title.en: Types of chemical reactions, oxidation, corrosion and rancidity

text.en: Quicklime added to water gets hot; a rusty iron nail turns brown; old oil smells bad. Each is a different kind of change. We classify reactions into types.

In a combination reaction two or more reactants form a single product, for example CaO + H2O gives Ca(OH)2 with release of heat, an exothermic reaction.
In a decomposition reaction one substance breaks into simpler ones, for example 2FeSO4 on heating gives Fe2O3 + SO2 + SO3, and 2Pb(NO3)2 gives 2PbO + 4NO2 + O2.
Decomposition can be by heat (thermal), light (photolytic) or electricity (electrolytic). Silver chloride turns grey in sunlight.
In a displacement reaction a more reactive element displaces a less reactive one from its compound: Fe + CuSO4 gives FeSO4 + Cu.
In double displacement, ions are exchanged: Na2SO4 + BaCl2 gives BaSO4 (white precipitate) + 2NaCl. A precipitation reaction forms an insoluble solid.
Oxidation is gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen. Reduction is loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen. Both happen together in a redox reaction.
Corrosion is the slow eating away of metals by air and moisture, for example rusting of iron and the green coating on copper.
Rancidity is the oxidation of fats and oils that makes food smell and taste bad. It is prevented by antioxidants, airtight containers and flushing with nitrogen.

problem.en: Identify the type: Zn + CuSO4 -> ZnSO4 + Cu.

text.en: Zinc is more reactive than copper.
Zinc takes the place of copper in the compound.
So it is a displacement reaction (and also a redox reaction).

why.en: Zn is oxidised, Cu2+ is reduced.

prompt.en: List the types of chemical reactions with examples.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking oxidation means only gain of oxygen

points.en: Types: combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement.
Oxidation is gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen; reduction is the opposite.
Corrosion and rancidity are oxidation processes in daily life.
